data.caption: therapetmd.com
data.copy:
I've been a dog trainer for 20 years.
And I need to confess something about puppy peeing...

We've been teaching puppy potty training all wrong.
And I'm partly to blame.

Let me explain.

Last month, a woman called me crying.
Her 4-month-old puppy was peeing inside constantly.

She was doing everything right.
Taking the puppy out every hour.
Praising when he peed outside.
Using enzyme cleaners.
Watching him like a hawk.

But he'd pee outside...
Come back in...
And pee again 20 minutes later.

She was ready to give up.

This happens twice a week in my practice.
And here's what I finally figured out after 20 years:

It's not a training problem.
It's a stress problem.

Most trainers won’t tell you this —
Because we make money from training classes.

But I’m done lying to people.

Your puppy isn’t being stubborn.
They’re scared.

Think about it.

New home.
New people.
New smells.
New routine.

Everything is terrifying for a baby dog.

And when they're terrified?
Their body loses control.

They start peeing inside to spread their scent.
Because their pee smells familiar.
It makes them feel safe.

So they’re literally peeing to self-soothe.

All that training you’re doing?
It can’t work yet.

Because their brain is in panic mode.

A stressed puppy can’t learn.
No matter how good your training is.

I learned this 5 years ago — and it changed everything.

I started using calming pheromone diffusers with my clients.
Specifically, TheraPet brand.

These release the same calming signals a mother dog gives her puppies.
It tells their brain:
"You're safe. This is home. You don’t need to mark."

I plug in 3–4 around the house.
Within 2–3 days? The change is dramatic.

The puppy stops sneaking off to pee.
They start actually holding it.
Accidents drop by 70–80%.

And here’s the crazy part —
All that training you’ve been doing suddenly starts working.

Because the puppy is finally calm enough to learn.

I’ve seen this work on golden retrievers.
